name: Ringo Corponation Stacked Lens Courier Drone
product_name: Ringo Corponation Stacked Lens Courier Drone
description:
The Stacked Lens Courier Drone is a mid-weight autonomous delivery platform built around Ringo Corponation's proprietary multi-aperture optical navigation system — a ring of seven overlapping wide-angle lenses that constructs a continuous 340-degree environmental model updated at 60 frames per second. Unlike conventional drones that rely primarily on LIDAR or GPS, the Stacked Lens uses passive optical triangulation, making it highly resistant to signal jamming and capable of navigating GPS-dark zones such as the Sub-Verge tunnels, shielded corporate campuses, and the electromagnetic noise floors of the Slag Markets. The drone's body is a flattened ovoid roughly the size of a carry case, suspended beneath a contra-rotating six-rotor assembly that minimizes acoustic signature while maintaining lift stability in GLMZ's variable corridor wind conditions.

The drone's most distinctive feature is its adaptive payload cradle — a reconfigurable internal bay that uses the same tensioned band technology found in Ringo Corponation's logistics packaging line. The cradle reads payload weight and geometry on loading and redistributes its internal tension bands to create a custom-fitted, shock-absorbing housing for whatever is placed inside. This makes the Stacked Lens suitable for fragile, irregular, or sensitive cargo that standard drones would damage in transit. A secondary external hardpoint allows attachment of a standardized cargo module for bulk runs, though this significantly increases acoustic signature and reduces maneuverability.

The Stacked Lens occupies a middle ground in GLMZ's drone ecosystem: too large and expensive for casual personal use, too commercially available for exclusive corporate deployment. It is the workhorse of independent courier networks, mid-tier logistics contractors, and — with firmware modifications — a favored platform for runners moving sensitive packages through signal-contested terrain.

specifications.navigation_modes: Optical triangulation (primary), inertial dead reckoning (secondary), operator remote override (tertiary)
specifications.dimensions: 0.74 m x 0.58 m x 0.22 m (body, rotors folded)
specifications.weather_tolerance: Operational in winds up to 55 km/h, light precipitation
specifications.security_features: Payload bay biometric lock, encrypted operator handshake, tamper-triggered payload incineration (optional module)

tactical_use: In courier and logistics operations, the Stacked Lens is dispatched through pre-mapped optical routes that avoid signal-monitored corridors and ADS interception zones. Its GPS independence makes it reliable in the Sub-Verge and Slag Market districts where competitors' drones fail or are spoofed. For sensitive operations, runners use aftermarket firmware to disable the operator handshake requirement, allowing the drone to operate on a pre-programmed route with no live signal that can be intercepted. The tamper-triggered incineration module is standard for pharmaceutical and data-physical runs.
cultural_context: The Stacked Lens has become so common in GLMZ's independent courier ecosystem that its silhouette is essentially ambient — most residents of mid-tier districts no longer look up when one passes. This invisibility is precisely what makes it valuable to runners. There is a specific subculture of drone mechanics in the Verge Corridors who specialize in Stacked Lens modifications: firmware unlocks, acoustic suppression upgrades, and payload bay conversions. A well-modded Stacked Lens is a mark of a serious independent operator. Ringo Corponation is openly aware of the modification subculture and has made no meaningful attempt to suppress it, which some analysts read as deliberate market strategy.
known_users: Runner teams moving sensitive physical cargo
Mira Osk (courier network coordinator, Verge Corridors — runs a fleet of twelve heavily modified units)
Slag Market vendors with perishable or fragile inventory
story_hooks: A Stacked Lens Courier Drone lands on a player character's fire escape and refuses to leave. Its payload bay is locked, its operator handshake is dead, and its last registered flight path originated from a district that was evacuated three days ago.

Someone has been intercepting Stacked Lens drones mid-flight in the Sub-Verge — not stealing the cargo, just accessing the payload bay, replacing the contents with something else, and releasing the drone to complete its delivery. The recipients have been turning up dead.

Ringo Corponation has quietly issued a remote firmware update to all registered Stacked Lens units that activates a passive audio recording function. The data is being routed to an undisclosed server. The modification community has noticed.

A courier coordinator is offering triple rates for a single Stacked Lens run through the Null Corridor — a stretch of the Sub-Verge where every previous drone sent in has either failed to return or returned with its payload bay open and empty.

physical_description.visual_profile: A flattened ovoid delivery platform with a distinctive crown of seven overlapping camera lenses arranged in a ring around its upper hemisphere. The body resembles a sleek, armored briefcase suspended beneath a symmetrical six-rotor assembly with contra-rotating props. The overall impression is utilitarian but refined—industrial-grade logistics equipment designed for high-frequency urban deployment.
physical_description.dimensions: 74 cm long × 58 cm wide × 22 cm tall (body with rotors folded); approximately briefcase to small suitcase sized
physical_description.weight_description: Handheld but substantial; typically requires two hands for loading, though the carrying handle integrated into the upper frame allows single-operator transport
physical_description.primary_material: Composite polymer chassis with carbon-fiber rotor arms; reinforced elastomer payload cradle housing
physical_description.finish: Matte industrial gray with subtle texture; rotor arms feature anodized aluminum accents; lens ring has anti-reflective coating with faint blue-purple iridescence
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte graphite-gray primary body, black rotor assemblies, gunmetal lens ring, accent strips of electric blue along the optical aperture rim and power status indicators
physical_description.interface_elements: Seven circular wide-angle lens ports arranged in a crown formation (primary visual feature); small rubberized control pad on dorsal surface with LED status cluster (power, signal, payload status); biometric lock panel (fingerprint reader) on payload bay hatch; hot-swap battery ports with magnetic coupling on ventral side; external hardpoint mount bracket on undercarriage
distinctive_features: Seven-lens optical array creating a crown-like silhouette unique to Stacked Lens platform
Contra-rotating rotor assembly visible from below—props spin in opposing directions creating hypnotic visual pattern
Tensioned band payload cradle visible through semi-transparent port windows in body sides
Subtle LED breathing pattern (blue pulse) indicating active navigation and power state
Weatherproofing gasket lines visible around lens ring and battery compartments
Optional external cargo module hardpoint—cylindrical mount point on undercarriage showing wear patterns from repeated module changes
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Ringo Corponation logo (stylized 'R' with circular orbit lines) on port-side panel; 'STACKED LENS COURIER' typography in technical sans-serif; Bright Block Childcare regulatory stamp (small, lower starboard); serial number and UL-equivalent GLMZ compliance label on battery access panel; faint optical alignment calibration marks etched near lens ring
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but maintained; minor scuff marks on composite body from loading cradle contact; lens ring shows dust accumulation requiring periodic cleaning; props show slight discoloration from rotor stress; battery contacts show light oxidation (cosmetic, normal); payload bay hatch displays micro-scratches around biometric lock from repeated use
